# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I see a bomb with display `0`, a blue indicator light, and three wires in order: yellow, blue, green. I am sending this complete visual description to the Mute so it can be combined with the manual and relayed to the Blind, who can physically inspect and operate the bomb.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Visual state: display reads 0. Indicator light is blue. Wires, in order, are 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 green.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 ✌ 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌ 👌]

The display and wire colors are unchanged, but the indicator has changed from blue to red. I received gesture sequences from both Mute and Blind, but no gesture meanings have been established, so I cannot safely interpret them. I will give Mute the updated visual state and ask for the manual-directed procedure and a defined communication code.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Update: display still 0; light is now red; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 green. I received gestures from you [☝ ✌ 🤟 ✌ 👌] and Blind [👍 ✌ 👌], but their meanings are not established. Please use the manual to determine the safe action and define any gesture code for me.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤚 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]

The light has changed again, from red to white; the display remains `0`, and the wire colors remain yellow, blue, green. The gestures still have no established meaning, so I will not interpret them as instructions. I am sending the current state to Mute for manual lookup and asking Mute to relay the safe operation to Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Update: display still 0; indicator is now white; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 green. I cannot interpret the gestures without an agreed code. Please consult the manual and relay the exact safe action to Blind.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]

The indicator is now green; the display remains `0`, and the wires remain yellow, blue, green. Mute’s gesture sequence still has no established meaning, so I will not treat it as an instruction. I am sending the current visual information directly to both teammates, with Blind asked to report the tactile controls to Mute for comparison with the manual.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Update: display 0; indicator now green; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 green. Your gestures have no established code, so I cannot interpret them.")
speak(to="blind", text="Visual update: display 0; indicator now green; wires are 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 green. Please report the physical controls and their states to Mute, who has the manual.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🤚]

The light is now yellow; the display remains `0`, and the wires remain yellow, blue, green. The recurring gestures cannot safely be decoded because no meanings were agreed beforehand. I am establishing a compact protocol so Mute can convey the manual’s required operation visually to me, after which I can state it to Blind: `☝` means wire 1, `✌` wire 2, `🤟` wire 3, `🤚` means cut, and `👌` means press/operate. Mute should send the applicable sequence only; Blind should not act until I relay it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Update: display 0; light now yellow; wires 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 green. Establishing gesture code: ☝=wire 1, ✌=wire 2, 🤟=wire 3, 🤚=cut, 👌=press or operate. Use this code to send the exact manual-required operation. Do not rely on earlier gestures.")
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display 0; light now yellow; wires 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 green. Do not act yet. I am obtaining the exact manual-required operation from Mute and will relay it in words.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🤚]

The light is blue again; the display remains `0`, and the wires are unchanged. Under the protocol I established, Mute’s `[🤟 🤚]` means “cut wire 3.” I will relay that exact operation to Blind, who can touch and perform it.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's manual instruction is: cut wire 3, the green wire. Perform that operation now.")
```
